episodes.title: Welcome to Chandamama — Uncle Moonbeam's Story House
episodes.subtitle: A warm introduction to the magical world of Chandamama

cast.name: Uncle Moonbeam
cast.description: The kindly moon uncle who has told stories to children for over fifty years.

cast.name: Little Star
cast.description: A curious child who asks the questions every listener wonders.

scenes.title: The Moonlit Terrace
scenes.setting: A soft silver terrace under a full moon, with cushions scattered about and a warm lantern glowing.

scenes.title: The Story of Chandamama
scenes.setting: A magical timeline showing India from 1947 to 1999, with magazine covers floating like fireflies.

scenes.title: The Promise
scenes.setting: A bridge of moonlight stretching across the world, connecting children of all nations.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Hello, my little stars! Can you hear me? I am Uncle Moonbeam, and I have been waiting for you.

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: Uncle Moonbeam! Is it really you? Mama says you live on the moon!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: I do indeed live on the moon, little one. And from up here, I can see every child on Earth who is ready for a story. Tonight, I see you.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: But before we begin our tale, let me tell you a story about stories. Long, long ago, in the year nineteen forty-seven, when India had just found her freedom, a magical magazine was born.

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: Nineteen forty-seven? That is before my grandmother was born!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Yes, indeed! It was called Chandamama. In Telugu, that means 'Moon Uncle.' In Sanskrit, we say Chandamama too, for the moon is everyone's uncle.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Every month, children across the subcontinent would wait with shining eyes for Chandamama to arrive. It came in Sanskrit, in Telugu, in Hindi, in Tamil, in Bengali, in Marathi, in Kannada, in Oriya — in so many tongues that I cannot count them on all my moon-rays.

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: What kind of stories, Uncle? Were they scary?

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Some were thrilling, yes! There were stories of King Vikramaditya and the clever Vetala, who asked impossible riddles. There were stories from the Ramayana and Mahabharata, painted so beautifully that you could smell the forest and hear the arrows fly.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: There were stories of animals who spoke like us — wise elephants, cunning foxes, brave lions. There were stories of great kings and humble farmers, of princesses and potters. But do you know what every single story carried?

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: What, Uncle?

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Ancient wisdom. Lessons of dharma — doing what is right, even when it is hard. Of ahimsa — kindness to all living things, from the smallest ant to the mightiest elephant. And of courage that comes in all sizes, not just the size of giants.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Now, from the December nineteen ninety-nine Sanskrit issue — carefully preserved on Archive dot org by kind people who love stories as much as we do — we are bringing these tales back to life.

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: But Uncle, I do not read Sanskrit!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: That is why I am here, little star! We are retelling these tales in eight languages. English, Telugu, Hindi, Chinese, Spanish, Italian, German, and French. And we are doing it as enacted podcasts, with different voices for each character, just like a play!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: You can listen on your phone, on a tablet, on a computer. You can read along with the transcript. You can even download the stories to listen on a long car ride. And best of all — it is completely free. Forever.

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: Free forever? Like the moonlight?

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Exactly like the moonlight, little one. No one can own the moonlight, and no one should own a good story. Now, snuggle up. The moon is full, the stars are bright, and our first tale is about to begin. Are you ready?

script.speaker: Little Star
script.text: I am ready, Uncle Moonbeam!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Then let us begin. But first, a little puzzle. Look at the moon tonight. Can you see the face of the old man in the moon? He is smiling at you. Goodnight, little stars. Until we meet again in the next story.

episodes.title: The King and the Queen — The Lamp of Dharma
episodes.subtitle: From the cover of December 1999: King Vikramaditya sees a mystery beyond the seven hills.

cast.name: Uncle Moonbeam
cast.description: The kindly storyteller who guides us through the tale.

cast.name: King Vikramaditya
cast.description: A wise and just king, brave as a lion, gentle as a lamb.

cast.name: Queen Ananya
cast.description: Curious, kind, and clever. She sees what others miss.

cast.name: Minister Gopal
cast.description: Cautious but loyal. He worries so the king does not have to.

cast.name: Old Sage
cast.description: Ancient, mysterious, and full of riddles.

scenes.title: The Royal Balcony at Dawn
scenes.setting: Marble balcony overlooking seven hills. First rays of sun paint gold and saffron across the sky.

scenes.title: The Throne Room
scenes.setting: Grand hall with sandstone pillars. Court gathers, whispers fill the air like autumn leaves.

scenes.title: The Eastern Road
scenes.setting: Dusty path through ancient banyan trees. Morning mist clings to the forest floor.

scenes.title: The Hermit's Cave
scenes.setting: A cave mouth hidden behind waterfalls. Crystals glitter in the dim light.

scenes.title: The Garden of Answers
scenes.setting: Moonlit garden where jasmine flowers glow like tiny lamps. The truth is hidden among the petals.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: In the ancient kingdom of Ujjain, there lived a king named Vikramaditya. He was known throughout the land for his wisdom, his justice, and his kindness to all creatures great and small.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: One crisp winter morning, as the first rays of dawn painted the sky in gold and saffron, the king stood upon his royal balcony, gazing far into the eastern hills.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: My dear Ananya, come quickly! Look there, beyond the seven hills. Do you see what I see?

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: What is it, my lord? I see only the morning mist rolling over the hills... wait. Is that... a light? A golden light, dancing upon the highest peak?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: Yes! It is no ordinary light. It pulses like a heartbeat. I believe it is the Lamp of Dharma, lost for three hundred years.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: The Lamp of Dharma? But my lord, that is only a legend told to children at bedtime. Are you certain?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: I am as certain as the sun rising in the east. The old texts say: 'When the Lamp returns, its light shall be seen from the balcony of the just king.' And look — the light answers my gaze. It flickers twice, then holds steady.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Then we must send an expedition at once. But who could brave the eastern hills? They are treacherous, my lord. The old forests, the cursed peaks...

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: That is why I shall go myself. The kingdom needs wisdom more than it needs a king who sits safely on his throne.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The king called his court to the throne room. Ministers, scholars, and soldiers gathered, their whispers filling the grand hall like the rustle of autumn leaves.

script.speaker: Minister Gopal
script.text: Your Majesty, with respect, the eastern hills are treacherous. The path is guarded by old forests where even brave men lose their way. And the mountain peak is said to be cursed by a forgotten sage.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: Cursed? Nonsense, Gopal. The only curse is the fear in our own hearts. But you are right about the danger. That is why I will take only those who volunteer — and a good supply of courage.

script.speaker: Captain Veer
script.text: Your Majesty! I volunteer. Where you lead, the guard follows. We shall cut through any forest, climb any peak, face any curse — if it means bringing the Lamp of Dharma back to Ujjain!

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Then I volunteer too, my lord. For where you go, I go. And I know a secret path through the eastern forest — a path shown to me by my grandmother, who was a forest healer. She called it the Path of the Listening Heart.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: The Path of the Listening Heart? I have never heard of such a path.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: That is because it cannot be found with eyes, my lord. It can only be found with the heart. One must listen to the forest — to the wind, to the birds, to the whisper of the leaves — and the path reveals itself.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so, at dawn the very next day, the royal party set out. The king, the queen, Captain Veer and three guards, and Minister Gopal — who complained the entire way but never turned back.

script.speaker: Minister Gopal
script.text: Are we there yet? My feet hurt. My back aches. And I am quite certain that tree just moved.

script.speaker: Captain Veer
script.text: Trees do not move, Minister. That was a monkey. A very large monkey. Please try to keep up.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Shh! Everyone, be still. Listen. Do you hear it? The wind is singing. Follow me.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The queen led them through the forest not by sight, but by sound. When the wind grew warm, they turned left. When the birds sang a particular melody, they turned right. When the stream bubbled in a rhythm like a heartbeat, they knew they were on the true path.

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: Ananya, you are extraordinary. I have ridden through this forest a hundred times and never noticed these signs.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: That is because you were looking, my lord. Sometimes we must close our eyes to truly see.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: At last, they reached the foot of the highest peak. But between them and the summit stood a waterfall, thundering down with the force of a thousand drums. Behind the waterfall, barely visible, was the mouth of a cave.

script.speaker: Captain Veer
script.text: Your Majesty, the waterfall is too strong. We cannot pass through it.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Wait. Look at the water. It is not just falling — it is speaking. Listen carefully.

script.speaker: Old Sage
script.text: Who seeks the Lamp of Dharma?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: I am Vikramaditya, King of Ujjain. I seek the Lamp to bring wisdom to my people.

script.speaker: Old Sage
script.text: Many have sought the Lamp. All have failed. For the Lamp does not shine for those who seek power. It shines only for those who seek truth. Tell me, King Vikramaditya — what is the greatest truth?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: The greatest truth is that we are all connected. The king and the beggar, the lion and the lamb, the mountain and the grain of sand. When I hurt another, I hurt myself. When I lift another, I rise too.

script.speaker: Old Sage
script.text: And what is the greatest lie?

script.speaker: King Vikramaditya
script.text: The greatest lie is that we are separate. That my happiness can exist while another suffers. That my kingdom can prosper while my neighbor starves.

script.speaker: Old Sage
script.text: Then you may pass. But know this — the Lamp you seek is not in this cave. It is in your heart. It has always been there. The light on the mountain was merely a reflection of the light you already carry.

script.speaker: Queen Ananya
script.text: Then why did we come all this way?

script.speaker: Old Sage
script.text: Because wisdom without journey is merely words. You had to walk the path to understand that the path was inside you all along. Go now. Return to Ujjain. And let your people see the Lamp that shines in your actions.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so, dear listeners, the king and queen returned to Ujjain. They brought no golden lamp, no magical treasure. But they brought something far more precious — the understanding that the light of dharma, of doing what is right, shines not in distant caves but in every kind act, every just decision, every moment of courage.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: King Vikramaditya ruled for many more years, and under his light, Ujjain became the brightest kingdom in all the land. Not because of gold or jewels, but because every person — from the highest minister to the lowest sweeper — carried a little of the Lamp in their heart.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And that, my little stars, is the true story of the King and the Queen. Now, look into your own heart. Can you feel a little light there? That is your Lamp of Dharma. Keep it burning bright. Goodnight.

episodes.title: Dr. Rabbit's Puzzle — The Maze of Friendship
episodes.subtitle: From pages 2–3 of December 1999: Help Smita find her way through the magical maze!

cast.name: Smita
cast.description: Six years old, brave as a lion cub, curious as a kitten.

cast.name: Dr. Rabbit
cast.description: A clever rabbit who is the best dentist in the forest.

cast.name: Mr. Squirrel
cast.description: Chatty, helpful, and always dropping hints.

cast.name: Butterfly Queen
cast.description: Graceful, magical, and speaks in riddles.

scenes.title: Smita's Colorful Village
scenes.setting: Houses painted in every rainbow color. Children playing, smells of fresh jalebi in the air.

scenes.title: The Whispering Woods
scenes.setting: Friendly forest where trees point the way and butterflies form arrows in the air.

scenes.title: The Butterfly Meadow
scenes.setting: A field of flowers where every bloom is a different color. Butterflies dance in patterns.

scenes.title: Dr. Rabbit's Burrow
scenes.setting: Cozy underground clinic with carrot-shaped chairs, warm fireplace, and shelves of herb jars.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: In a little village where the houses were painted in every color of the rainbow, there lived a girl named Smita. She was six years old, brave as a lion cub, and curious as a kitten.

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: Smita, my little sunshine, it is time for your visit to Dr. Rabbit. Remember, he lives on the other side of the Whispering Woods.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: But Mama, the Whispering Woods are so big! What if I get lost?

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: You will not get lost, my brave girl. Dr. Rabbit left a puzzle for you. If you solve it, the path will open like a flower. Here, look at this map.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Smita looked at the map. It was no ordinary map. It was a maze! A beautiful, winding maze drawn in carrot ink on birch bark.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: I see three paths! The red path goes through the Thorny Thicket. The blue path crosses the Bubbling Brook. And the green path winds through the Butterfly Meadow. Which one is right, Mama?

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: Dr. Rabbit's note says: 'Choose the path where friends help friends, where flowers smile, and where the water sings.'

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Friends help friends... flowers smile... water sings... I know! The green path through Butterfly Meadow! Butterflies are friends to flowers, and the meadow has a singing stream!

script.speaker: Mama
script.text: That is my clever girl. But remember — the maze is not just about finding the right path. It is about who you meet along the way. Every friend you make is a clue. Every kindness you give is a key.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so Smita set off, her little boots crunching on the forest path. The Whispering Woods were not scary at all — they were whispering encouragement! 'You can do it, little one,' rustled the leaves. 'We believe in you,' creaked the branches.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Hello, Mr. Squirrel! Have you seen Dr. Rabbit's burrow?

script.speaker: Mr. Squirrel
script.text: Chitter-chatter! Yes, yes, little human! But I cannot tell you directly. Dr. Rabbit says I must only give clues. Here is your clue: I drop nuts where the path is true. Follow the acorns!

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Follow the acorns? But you drop acorns everywhere!

script.speaker: Mr. Squirrel
script.text: Not everywhere! Only where the moss is soft and the mushrooms grow in circles. Those are the true places. The other acorns are just snacks!

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Smita looked carefully. Indeed, some acorns lay on hard dry ground, while others rested on soft green moss near fairy-ring mushrooms. She followed the moss-path, and soon the forest opened into the most beautiful sight she had ever seen.

script.speaker: Butterfly Queen
script.text: Welcome, little traveler. I am the Butterfly Queen. We have been waiting for you. The flowers whispered that a brave girl would come today.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: You were waiting for me? But you do not even know me!

script.speaker: Butterfly Queen
script.text: We know kindness when we see it. You helped the old tortoise cross the path. You shared your lunch with the hungry sparrow. You spoke gently to the frightened fawn. The forest sees everything, little one. And the forest remembers.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: I did not do those things to be remembered. I did them because... because it felt right.

script.speaker: Butterfly Queen
script.text: That is exactly why the Lamp of Dharma shines in your heart, Smita. Now, we shall dance you across the meadow. Follow our wings. But beware — the wind will try to blow you toward the Thorny Thicket. Do not let it. Hold onto kindness, and you will not fall.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: The butterflies formed a bridge of color — orange and blue and gold and purple — and Smita walked across the meadow as if she were walking on a rainbow. The wind howled and tugged, but she thought of the tortoise, the sparrow, and the fawn, and her feet stayed firm.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: At last, she reached a round green door with a carrot-shaped knocker. She knocked three times.

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: Well, well, well! If it isn't little Smita! I see you solved my puzzle. The green path of friendship and kindness. That is always the right path, you know. Not the shortest. Not the easiest. But always the right one.

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: I did it, Dr. Rabbit! And the woods helped me. Mr. Squirrel showed me the moss-path, and the Butterfly Queen danced me across the meadow!

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: That is because you have a kind heart, Smita. Kind hearts always find their way. Now, let us look at those teeth. Open wide and say 'ahhh'!

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Ahhhh!

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: Perfect! Strong and shiny, just like your courage. Here is a carrot for being the bravest patient of the day. And remember, brush twice a day — morning and night! A clean tooth is a happy tooth!

script.speaker: Smita
script.text: Thank you, Dr. Rabbit! Can I come back through the maze again tomorrow?

script.speaker: Dr. Rabbit
script.text: The maze is always open to those with kind hearts, Smita. But tomorrow, try a different path. See what new friends you meet. Every day, the maze changes — because every day, you change.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: And so, dear little listeners, Smita walked home with a carrot in her hand, a smile on her face, and a new lesson in her heart: when you are kind and brave, the whole world helps you find your way. The maze was never about reaching Dr. Rabbit's burrow. It was about discovering that kindness is the only map you ever truly need.

script.speaker: Uncle Moonbeam
script.text: Now, who is ready to draw their own maze? And remember — put plenty of friends along the path. Goodnight, little stars!
